name: Cross-recurrence quantification (CRQA)
title: Do two series visit the same states, and when?
what: Turn two series into states and count how often they are in matching states, at each lead or lag.
pick_line: An order-aware test with familywise lag control and persistence-matched surrogates.
data: Public aggregates (OFR repo, NY Fed fails, Form PF); descriptive only
one: Fails and the rate spread move in step the same week (p = 0.011), but not after July 2025.

left.sub: rolling windows significant: full-plot RR ignores order, so every shift ties

right.sub: windows significant, about 5 expected by chance

findings.h: High fails come with a low DVP rate, in the same week.
findings.t: Same-week anti-recurrence of financing fails and the DVP–tri-party spread: 0.287 vs 0.20 by chance (p = 0.011). No lead either way (asymmetry p = 0.56).

findings.h: The coupling was on from 2019 to mid-2025, then switched off.
findings.t: Same-week coupling was significant in 52 of 96 rolling years, and in none of the 15 windows ending after July 2025, which cover the late-2025 fails spike.

chart.title: Rolling years with p < 0.05 (of 96)
rows: Same-week rate, fails vs DVP growth

findings.note: Windows overlap, so counts are descriptive.

findings.h: Form PF reverse-repo borrowing leads DVP volume by about 4 months.
findings.t: Familywise p = 0.001 (asymmetry p = 0.001). Prime-broker borrowing shows no link that survives the max over lags.
findings.note: * not significant after 8 tests. Form PF is published about two quarters late: a lead in reference month, not in time to act.
